abstract.para: The oscap command scans a system against the rules of a profile from the &ssg;. The command saves the results in the Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF) and can generate an HTML report.

section.title: Installing the packages
section.para: The openscap-utils package provides the oscap and autotailor commands. The scap-security-guide package provides the profiles. To install both packages, run the following command:

section.title: Scanning against a profile
section.para: The following procedure scans the local system against the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) profile. For more information about the other profiles, see .

step.para: To scan the system and generate a report, run the following command:

callout.para: Scans the system without changing it.
Specifies the profile. You can also use the short form hipaa.
Saves the results in XCCDF format.

step.para: The scan takes about one minute and prints the result of each rule, for example:
step.screen: Title Verify File Hashes with RPM Rule xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_rule_rpm_verify_hashes Ident CCE-96299-3 Result pass

step.para: To view the results, open /tmp/report.html in a Web browser.
The report starts with a summary, followed by the details of each rule. shows the summary for a system that has not been hardened.

section.para: In scripts, use the exit code of oscap to check the result of a scan. Exit code 0 means that no rule fails, 2 means that at least one rule fails and 1 means that the scan cannot run.
